newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer redeems Moyne K-shrs, plans conversion.
newsitem.headline: Amer redeems Moyne K-shrs, plans conversion.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Tuesday it had exercised its right to redeem 275,000 K shares offered to British investor Lord Moyne by one of four domestic institutions controlling the vote-strong K series.

Amer said its board would propose to an extraordinary shareholders meeting on August 26 that all K shares would be converted into its listed series A shares at a ratio of one-and-a-half A share for each K share.
"Decisions on corporate administration, strategy, dividend policy and management will be taken on the basis of A shareholder votes not K shareholder votes as is the case today," it said.

Amer said its board of directors had decided to exercise the redemption right because "the future success of the company, the stabilisation of its operations and in particular the loyalty of key personnel, requires the current uncertainty...to be eliminated."
Amer redeemed the K shares offered to Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne, by the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration (KY) for 75.3 million markka.
This would equal 273.82 markka per share. Amer's A share, suspended on Tuesday morning, on Monday closed at 91.30 markka.
